speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Today, I will bring Members through the key considerations behind these decisions: first, the importance of local news media to our nation and how we have upheld it through our history; second, the Government's reasons for supporting SPH's proposal; and third, our commitment to help our local news media adapt and thrive in the digital era.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Our local media is keenly attuned to our unique circumstances as a small city-state, an open economy and a multi-racial society.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: They help interpret global events through a distinctively Singaporean lens, analysing their impact on our lives.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: This is ever more crucial in an era of heightened geopolitical contestation.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The local media also express our identity, values and priorities so that the world gets a perspective from Singapore itself and not through the filter of others.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Domestically, the local media not only report on events and developments but also publish a balanced range of views to inform the national debate and help foster a national consensus, not allowing disagreements to deepen into divisions in our society.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: They help to sustain the common ground in our multi-racial and multi-religious society whilst preserving the voice of each of our communities through the vernacular media and they write "the first draft of our history", as Mr Goh Chok Tong put it in 1995, serving as an authoritative record of our collective experience as a people, giving future generations of Singaporeans a sense of how we saw the world, what was important to us and how we built tomorrow's Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The local news media fulfil this role while upholding high standards of accuracy, objectivity and balance.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: These are traits that are ever more scarce in the raucous global information landscape, especially online.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The local media help to distinguish fact from falsehood, substance from posture, "what is high from what is low", as Mr Lee Kuan Yew put it in 1998.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: As our nation faces increasingly complex challenges and trade-offs, our local media provide a highly credible flow of information and analysis upon which we form collective decisions.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: In the pandemic, Singaporeans looked to our local newspapers and channels as their trusted sources of critical information.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: In the UK, by comparison, YouGov found that only three in 10 trusted the information on COVID-19 in British newspapers.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Our local media industry has strived to do so while adapting to changing industry trends and commercial imperatives.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Because of its importance to the national interest, the Government has been an active steward in this evolutionary process to ensure the vitality and viability of our local media industry.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The primary aim of this merger nearly four decades ago was to preserve the vernacular media.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The Government could see that the vernacular papers would come under greater financial pressure over the years with the gradual shift towards English.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: As Mr Lee Kuan Yew explained at Lianhe Zaobao's 80th anniversary in 2003, "My worry as Prime Minister was how to preserve at least one quality Chinese newspaper and sustain it over the long term when the trend in education was towards English." The merger reduced duplication of overheads and costs of competition, and enabled the SPH newspapers to achieve economies of scale and greater commercial viability.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Between 2000 and 2005, the print and broadcast industries launched into more direct competition but subsequently re-consolidated.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Initially, SPH and Mediacorp were allowed to enter each other's main businesses, with the trend towards convergence between print and broadcast.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The hope was that greater competition between them would spur both to develop better local content and retain local audiences against rising foreign competition.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The competition was fierce but ultimately the model did not prove to be viable.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Against the backdrop of the dotcom crash and SARS, the industry was rationalised in 2004 to preserve the viability of the two companies; one a core broadcaster and the other a core newspaper group.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Sweeping structural changes in the media and advertising industries caused by technological advances and the Internet have severely disrupted the traditional business model that relied on print advertising revenue.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: In the borderless online space, our local news media must now compete not just with international news organisations but also entertainment providers and user-generated content.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The cost of producing quality news content remains high but revenues have plummeted.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Meanwhile, news aggregators and other news providers are now able to provide so-called "free news services" without the cost of maintaining a high-quality newsroom.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Though digital ads are growing, it is the digital platforms like social media and search engines that capture the lion's share of the revenue.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Though the demand for quality news has not diminished, monetising digital initiatives is challenging and the revenues of quality news platforms all over the world are falling sharply with little prospect of relief.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Just last week on World Press Freedom Day, the executive director of the World Association of News Publishers, Andrew Heslop, published an article quite aptly titled "Media across the globe fighting immediate and existential threats".

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: He warned, "Many of the difficult questions facing the news industry are underpinned by an inability to predict a general economic model that will guarantee a future for quality, professional journalism...

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The harsh reality: public interest reporting simply does not convert to advertising dollars." For many media companies, the economic fall-out of COVID-19 was the final straw.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: An article in the Columbia Journalism Review described it as "The Journalism Crisis Across the World".

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Most publications are now running deficits and many newsrooms are shrinking, even closing.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Southeast Asia has seen well-known newspapers change hands, restructure or shut down in recent years.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The Jakarta Globe ceased printing and went fully online in 2015 and the Philippine Star had a majority stake acquired by the telecommunications group, PLDT.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Ours is a small local market with just two main local news media organisations, SPH and Mediacorp.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: While there are potential synergies and opportunities for collaboration between them, we can ill afford the convulsions and closures we have seen elsewhere, with a consequential loss of diversity and choice in our media landscape.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The response of media companies across the world has been varied, reflecting their own social and political contexts.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Many have resorted to cost cutting to survive.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: It is now embarking on a consolidation exercise which will likely entail major cost cuts and job losses.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Even digital news sites which have ridden the wave of Internet media have not been spared.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Popular site, Buzzfeed, which claimed a greater online audience than the print circulation of any single newspaper, has never made a profit and was compelled to abort its global expansion plans last year.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Some publications have received life support from wealthy financial backers or funds.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Billionaires have acquired established newspapers for philanthropic or other motivations.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The Washington Post was bought by Jeff Bezos of Amazon in 2013, after 80 years of ownership by the Graham family, which had sustained the paper partly on the proceeds of its Kaplan education business.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The South China Morning Post (SCMP) was owned by Rupert Murdoch's News Corp until 1993, when it was acquired by Malaysian real estate tycoon Robert Kuok.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: In 2016, it was acquired by the Alibaba Group.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: With the largesse of Alibaba, SCMP lifted the paywall on its articles and was reported to have increased its international reach more than fourfold within three years.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: In 2020, SCMP restored the paywall and subscription model, acknowledging that the "advertising model is no longer enough to sustain high-quality news".

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Other major newspapers now owned by billionaires include the Los Angeles Times.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Even hedge funds have got into the act.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Alden Global Capital acquired over 200 US newspapers, with extensive lay-offs and cost-cutting measures.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Some newspapers have received funding from non-profit organisations.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The Guardian in the UK has been owned by the Scott Trust since 1936.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: It has done well against global competition – nearly two-thirds of its readers come from outside the UK.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: But in 2020, after making a £25 million pound loss even after drawing from the Trust, The Guardian announced plans to cut 12% of its workforce saying that "we face unsustainable annual losses in future years unless we take decisive action." Even the rare papers that are profitable are under continuing pressure.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The Wall Street Journal has had to make numerous changes to its operating model to keep afloat.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: While investing in a special innovation team of 150 employees, it has also had to thin out its print edition and lay off staff as recently as 2016.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The New York Times' success is not easy to replicate.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Beyond digital transformation, it commands a global attention that is difficult for our media, writing from the perspective of a small country, to emulate.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: It is also noteworthy that the New York Times and Washington Post tripled their digital subscriptions during the period of the Trump administration.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Meanwhile, US metropolitan dailies of comparable size, like the LA Times, Chicago Tribune and San Francisco Chronicle, have seen significant falls in circulation, in part because of "subscription fatigue" among readers.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The Financial Times (FT), which enjoys the advantage of being a specialist newspaper, employs rigorous data analysis to tailor its coverage and subscription offers at its target segments.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: It has a small but affluent readership, exemplified by FT's weekly lifestyle magazine called "How to Spend It", with strong advertising appeal.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Still, in 2015, the Japanese media group Nikkei bought FT from Britain's Pearson.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: So, even a successful newspaper is susceptible to takeover.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Governments around the world have recognised the news media as a public good that merits direct public funding.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Less well-known is public funding of print media, but it has a long tradition in European countries.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The French government spends hundreds of millions of euros annually to support the press, including prominent papers like Le Monde and Le Figaro.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: It has done so for over half a century, with annual subsidies at times exceeding a billion euros.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Scandinavian governments too have supported their newspapers for decades, both through direct subsidies and tax breaks.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: In 2020 alone, the Norwegian Media Authority gave press subsidies of 43 million euros, while Sweden rendered a 65-million euro aid package to buffer the impact of the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: In Singapore, we provide annual funding for public service broadcasting to Mediacorp.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: So, in sum, the global news media industry is under severe structural pressure and there is no universal solution.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: A few have succeeded; some are struggling; many have failed.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The sources of support – be it public, private, philanthropic or others – have varied widely.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: And at this critical juncture, SPH Media must similarly chart its own course to revise and, if necessary, re-invent its business model for the digital age.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Against these industry headwinds, SPH has held out longer than most.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: In fact, SPH's overall reach and readership has never been higher.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: It has augmented newsrooms with a wider range of tech capabilities, such as product development, digital content production, data analytics and audience development.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: It has modified its operations to generate content round the clock and deployed it on a wider variety of social media platforms, including Instagram and Telegram.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: SPH has launched new platforms for readers to engage its correspondents and experts and has been recognised internationally for its excellent data visualisation and interactive graphics, multimedia and photojournalism.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Last year, it emerged as the biggest winner at the Asian Media Awards, with The Straits Times and the Chinese Media Group picking up accolades in breaking news, infographics, feature photography and newspaper design, to name a few.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: So, in short, these are not news platforms that are declining in quality or readership.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: On the contrary, like Mediacorp in broadcasting, SPH papers continue to be trusted and valued sources of news that are well read which is a tribute to the professionalism of our journalists.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Their challenge today stems from an inability to monetise their gains in attracting and retaining readers on digital platforms.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Despite rising readership, SPH's media business has been steadily losing revenue.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: And that loss would have been deeper without the Government's JSS grant.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Looking ahead, SPH expects these trends to persist and widen.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Print advertising revenue will continue falling as media consumption progressively shifts online.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Rising digital advertising revenue will not compensate for the fall in print advertising revenue.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: And there is limited scope to grow digital subscriptions given our small domestic market and the global competition.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: They affect SPH, Mediacorp and the global media industry.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: And the adverse effects will be compounded by the lingering economic impact of COVID-19, with businesses cutting ad spending and consumers reluctant to pay for content.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: SPH has been under persistent pressure to account to shareholders for the anaemic financial performance of its media business.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Hence, the company has implemented several cost-cutting and retrenchment exercises in recent years.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: But SPH has assessed that any further cuts would impair its ability to maintain quality journalism.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: SPH has also spoken of its constraints as a listed company to make significant and sustained investments in their digital and newsroom capabilities, which may not yield near-term payoffs.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Hence, under the current structure, there is a serious risk that SPH's media capabilities will be hollowed out.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Without sustained investment in capacity building and a digital pivot, its quality and circulation will fall.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: This, in turn, will worsen financials and cause further disinvestment.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: And the immediate pressure will inevitably be on our vernacular papers, some with relatively small circulations, which would have a profound detrimental impact on the multi-racial fabric of our society.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Without a responsible and high quality local media, the quality of our public debate and discourse will be compromised and we will slowly but inexorably become less cohesive as a society.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Given what is at stake, the Government must take a long-term view and adopt measures to secure the sustainability of our local media.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The Government therefore carefully studied the proposal from SPH.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Subsequently, if SPH shareholders give their approval, the subsidiary will be transferred to the CLG.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The CLG will be separate from the listed company, no longer run by the SPH management.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: It will operate as a revenue-seeking business, subject to the usual commercial disciplines.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: However, any operating surplus will be ploughed back into the media business, rather than distributed to shareholders as dividends.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: In that sense, it will be "not-for-profit" to the members of the CLG.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: This concept of a CLG run with commercial discipline is not new for us.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: There are several examples, including our Universities, The Esplanade and Gardens by the Bay.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: SPH's proposal is not a panacea for the challenges faced by its news media business.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: But it is an essential first step if the media business is to adapt to the digital and commercial realities of the industry.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Throughout our history, the Government has aimed to develop and sustain such a media industry in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: However, the current SPH model of a news media business within a listed company is no longer viable.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: While the media business' traditional revenues streams are declining sharply, significant investments are needed to build digital and other capabilities for the longer term.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: A Company Limited by Guarantee (CLG) is one model to remove the news media business from the constraints of a listed company, while the news business under the CLG invests in strategic imperatives.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: But the CLG will still have to find new sources of funding to meet the expected financial shortfalls in the news business.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We already have a similar financing model with Mediacorp, our core national broadcaster, which has been working well.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Having such national broadcasters, newspaper publishers and online news platforms is a public good that benefits the whole of society.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Although the business and financing model will change, the Government does not intend nor expect this to affect the relationship between MCI and the SPH newsroom.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The Government is mindful that our local news media must remain credible institutions that are trusted by Singaporeans and that it remains the responsibility of the editors and journalists in SPH Media to report news and diverse opinions objectively, and from a Singaporean point of view.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: First, strong leadership, with the support of its stakeholders, to set the strategic vision and execute the organisational transformation.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Second, a robust business strategy that can be sustained under the new structure with the requisite resources.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Third, a strong and capable team of professionals in the newsrooms, who will maintain the high standards that we have come to expect of this cherished national news organisation.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: In this regard, the Newspaper and Printing Presses Act (NPPA) is a key regulatory instrument that will apply to the news entities under the CLG.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: It places restrictions on the ownership and control of local newspaper companies.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Among other requirements, newspaper companies like SPH are required to issue two classes of shares: ordinary shares and management shares.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Ordinary shareholders can each hold no more than 5% of the company’s shares except with the approval of the Minister.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: This prevents excessive influence over local newspapers from any single source, local or foreign.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Management shareholders have special voting rights on resolutions relating to the appointment of directors and staff of the newspaper company.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The issuance of management shares and the appointment of directors must be approved by the Minister.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The intent has always been for these management shares to be held by reputable and established institutions, so that the stewardship of the newspaper is entrusted to entities with an abiding interest in and commitment to Singapore’s stability and success.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Currently, the management shareholders of SPH are OCBC, Great Eastern, UOB, DBS, Singtel, NTUC Income, Temasek via Fullerton Pte Ltd, NUS and NTU.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: As SPH restructures its media operations, we want to ensure that its management shareholders continue serving as custodians of the CLG.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: I have therefore met and consulted the representatives of the management shareholders.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: They have all agreed to form the CLG and to be its founding members.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: This will ensure that our local news media will remain in the hands of trusted institutions with a long-term stake in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: In due course, the membership will be expanded to include newer and more diverse institutions as stakeholders of the CLG.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: One important and immediate decision for the CLG is the appointment of the Chairman of its Board.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We want to ensure the CLG has the wherewithal to innovate, build digital and other essential capabilities, and confidently take on new challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We expect that after the transfer of the media business, the CLG will formulate detailed proposals on its strategic plan to build the business.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: This will form the basis for Government funding and support.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: On the regulatory front, the Government will maintain the safeguards hitherto placed on the media business under the NPPA.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The NPPA will not apply to the CLG, but appropriate safeguards will be incorporated in the constitution of the CLG to ensure that the CLG structure achieves its purpose and fosters the objectives of the NPPA framework; and that its members and directors will remain committed to Singapore’s stability and success.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: As I said at the beginning of this Statement, a high-quality, professional and trusted media, with news reported by Singaporeans for Singaporeans, is essential to the fabric of our nation.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Within the framework of the NPPA, the local media operate independently of the Government.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: They report and analyse the news fully and objectively, not holding back bad news, nor advancing any singular ideological view or agenda, but focused on Singapore’s interest.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The Government and the media will not see eye-to-eye on every issue and incident, but that is to be expected.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: That is how SPH and Mediacorp, have operated hitherto, and that is how the Government expects the CLG to continue to operate after the proposed restructuring.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The CLG must maintain the reputation and high level of trust that SPH has built with generations of readers, domestically and internationally.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: But we are convinced that it is essential if our news media are to survive as high-quality news outlets.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: And the Government will do our part to sustain a trusted news media in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: They are cherished institutions that reflect our values; whose "past, present and future are intrinsically tied to this nation", as Prime Minister Lee put it at The Straits Times’ 170th anniversary.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The newsrooms are, and must continue to be, home to talented editors and journalists, whose professionalism and diligence have built credibility and trust in our newspapers.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: As 19-year-old "A" level graduate Keng Xin Yi said in today's Straits Times and, I quote, "It is important to keep SPH Media alive and motivated to produce quality newspapers every day.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: ST has been serving Singaporeans with diligence and high standards, educating us from the time when we knew little about the world.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: I hope we can express our gratitude by supporting and respecting these dedicated journalists.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Together we can keep our source of knowledge going and keep our ST alive.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: I want ST to be a part of the lives of my future children and grandchildren too." Sir, the success of this restructuring and the future of our local news media, turn ultimately on our journalists' commitment to this mission and the support of our citizens like Xin Yi.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I have a few clarifications for the Minister.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Before that, I thank him for his Statement, which contained a lot of information or some information at least, that the public has heard for the first time today and here in the House.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Does the Ministry consider this contribution to be a reasonable one and how did it come to this conclusion?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I will attempt to give him a comprehensive response.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But I imagine this is going to be further developed in subsequent clarifications.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: First, on the issue of timing – when did we inform SPH that we were willing to fund SPH?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: As I said in my Statement, the Government has always taken the position that we are willing to support investments in capability development.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And then, it is up to the respective organisations to develop their plan and to put forward their proposals to us.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In addition, we were prepared to offer extra help if it was required, but the restructuring proposal was put to us; which then, leads to the next question about other sources of funding and whether Government funding to the CLG will be capped.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The reason for this is not because we are reluctant to talk about them, but it is simply because, first, this is still a matter before the shareholders of SPH.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: They have to decide whether they want to approve this.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It is only after that that we can really get into a more detailed discussion.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But it is not just about the shareholders' approval.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We also need the new CLG to then formulate its plans and put on the table what it sees as its strategic business direction, going forward; and in that matrix, the different sources of revenues that it expects or anticipates, and what role will the Government funding play in that matrix.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, the question of whether other sources of funding would be required, if the Leader of the Opposition heard in my speech 	earlier, not-for-profit does not mean that the entity does not pursue its business on a commercial basis.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Again, Mr Deputy Speaker, I want to stress that because this is a matter that has to be put to the shareholders at an Extraordinary General Meeting (EGM), I do not want to pre-empt any case that the management and the Board will make.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But I can say that our focus, the Government's focus, has been very clearly on the news media business and its viability, going forward.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And that is why we need to be clear that the Government will be prepared to come in to give support.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But how much, how – I think these are the things that will need to be worked out in due course after the CLG has had the chance, subject to shareholders' approval, to then develop a business plan and put the proposal to us.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The Member asked about structures for editorial independence or ensuring a culture of editorial independence.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I would venture that that culture already exists in Singapore in the news media.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think we do a disservice to our journalists and editors to suggest anything to the contrary.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In fact, if you look at the overall outcome that we have achieved over the years, it speaks to, not just from external sources that validate by recognising the accomplishments of our local news media but, importantly, and this has a bearing on the Leader of the Opposition's last point on the Select Committee, because if I understand it correctly, it is about enabling people to express their views.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I would say Singaporeans have already expressed their views because, first, when it comes to trust surveys, Singapore scores highly.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Singaporeans have been quick to point out that they trust our news media, both print and broadcast, and they have shared this.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And that is at a higher level than the trust they accord to international media, I would add.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, it is not just what they say though, it is also what they are doing.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: What are their habits, what are their preferences.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In other words, how are they voting with, in this case, their eyeballs?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The fact is, as I said, and I want to re-emphasise, the SPH news organisations, in aggregate, have not just maintained but they have grown their reach and readership, when you combine the digital and the physical.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: That would not be the case if Singaporeans did not feel that they could trust a news organisation.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, I think the people have spoken and it is our job now to make sure that object of their trust continues to succeed.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I have a couple of supplementary questions for the Minister.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: First of all, the Government will provide funding to the new entity, the new CLG called SPH Media.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is reasonable, if you provide the funding, to have some expectations, to have some accountability, even to have some conditions.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Can the Minister, perhaps, develop on what are some of the accountabilities or even the KPIs that the Government would expect from the new CLG in return for the funding?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And, of course, with that accountability, with that expectation, there could also be the criticism that, therefore, that is the way also of exerting control over the CLG.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Could the Minister, perhaps, also expound on some measures that could be put in place to balance off between expecting accountability but yet, at the same time, having a hands-off approach and not necessarily shaping or influencing how the CLG would then do its business?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: First, on accountability and conditions or KPIs tied to the funding.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Again, I want to start by saying this is still a matter that has to be approved by the shareholders of SPH before we can start talking about these matters in greater detail.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But I can talk about it in terms of broad principles.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It means that if the funding is given for a specific purpose, then the expectation, and in this case is for building capabilities, for example.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And the expectation must be that those capabilities are indeed developed.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It is something that both Mediacorp and the SPH news groups have been doing with significant success over the years.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But, clearly, it is something that we would want them to continue to strive to achieve.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: On the point about control, I think I had said some of this in my earlier response.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: First, let me acknowledge that it is inevitable that whenever you have a change, in this case, a structural change in the organisation, such concerns will naturally arise.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It is inevitable and it is quite understandable.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But as we deliberate on this and we discuss this in this Chamber, we also need to keep in mind where are we starting from when thinking about the future.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We are starting from a position where we have two news organisations, media organisations: one a core newspaper group with radio and online presence; another, a core broadcaster with radio and online presence.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: These organisations have developed under our existing model.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And what I mean by that is SPH is subject to the NPPA and the restrictions that go with it.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mediacorp gets funding from the Government in the form of public service broadcasting.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In both cases, they have been able to pursue their editorial policy in a manner that has allowed them to win the trust of Singaporeans, as evinced by the various studies and surveys, and so on, and also the reading habits of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, if I may put it another way, "If it ain't broke, don't fix it".

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The part that is challenging is the financial model, in particular.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The Minister spoke about the impact of digital disruptions on the news media industry.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: While digital investments and funding are important to maintain quality local news media, this clearly is not enough.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: In fact, SPH has actually grown its digital footprint as well as its viewership.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: So, what will be different for the CLG to achieve the digital pivot, that the Minister has said is required?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: A clear strategy to transform and to drive digital innovation is required and so, how will this new entity achieve that?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: My second question is a different one but an important one to maintaining the quality of local journalism, and that is really its people.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: In this case, it is the journalists themselves as well as the experienced team that produces the content.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: So, what is being done to ensure that that this retention of talent is there, as well as, more importantly, the ability for the new entity to attract new talent required for it to do the pivots it requires?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Perhaps, I will start with the people question first.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: One cannot talk about quality journalism without talking about quality journalists.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And indeed, when we talk about investing in the capability of our news media, this is one of the key attributes – the ability to attract, retain and develop journalistic talent which take our news media industry forward, both for the quality of its news reporting and also for its analysis of global and local events; and to be able to offer that distinctly Singapore perspective, which we need for all the reasons that I have outlined.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, we are very clear that when it comes to the people element, it is something that must continue to be supported.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: How that is done is a matter that the company itself must take forward.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And what I mean by this is, for example, if we think back to the Jobs Support Scheme (JSS), the objective was very simple – to prevent attrition of capabilities that have been developed and that are needed for the future.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But what we need in the context of SPH now is not just the prevention of attrition but actually, the ability to build on that capability which I think is the point that the Member makes as well.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And so, I think this is an area the new CLG Chairman, the Board and the management will be seized with.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And I would imagine that as part of their strategic business review that human dimension is going to be key because ultimately, that is what sustains the news media.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Having said that, the earlier point about what will be different, and I agree with the Member, financial support or money alone is not enough.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think really, it is about what you are using these resources for and therefore, what will be different.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I would say that the other thing is, again, I think the point that the Member makes – and the Member will be very familiar with this – is that it is not just about technology.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It is how that technology is applied in the context of this vertical and how it is used to deliver a product that is valued by the customers, the readers and whether there are different ways to find new revenue sources arising from that.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, this is a very important area of work.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I know that within the current SPH system, they have put some degree of effort into it.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: How did we arrive at the CLG structure and were alternatives considered?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And this, I want to emphasise again, is a proposal that awaits shareholders' approval.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, I do not want to go into a detailed discussion on its merits.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But as I have said quite clearly, the Government supports it.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We are supporting it not because of the shareholder value proposition.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, other ideas, whether it is privatisation and other formulations, I think these are questions that I am sure the Board and management would have considered.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But I also want to point out that from the Government's point of view, the regulatory levellers are quite specific.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: They only pertain to decisions that affect the news media business in the way I have explained.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, I think the larger issues around the business, its viability, its decisions on what can be done for shareholder value, ultimately, is something that the Board and management have to decide on and propose to shareholders to agree.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think the Member asked the question: is it possible for us to support the company in its present form, I assume, with something like public service broadcasting funding and so on.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Because I understand the intent of the Member.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In other words, the business is within the listed company.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Can we just direct the funding to that operation in that business for it to succeed?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And so, then it means, do we need to find other constructs to do with it.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And I do not want to belabour the point but other than to say that I do not think it is a straightforward solution.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think it is fraught in its own way.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: What we have before us is the proposal that the Board and management of SPH put to us after their own deliberations of various possibilities.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Our lens is purely from the point of view of how do we ensure a quality, professional trusted news media continues to succeed in Singapore.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And that is the basis on which we have expressed our approval for the restructuring.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: First, I would like to say that I welcome the Minister's statement in his speech that the Government and SPH Media will not see eye-to-eye on matters and it is as it should be if the newspapers are to be credible to readers.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The second question, does Minister not see this as a missed opportunity in the light of the major restructure that is coming up and some concerns about what this will mean for newspaper content?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Is this not a missed opportunity where someone else who is not so closely linked to the Government could have been chosen to be the Chairman?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I said in my Statement that the news media and the Government will not always see eye-to-eye.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I will think the definition of a good news media or a credible news media is that it must always not see eye-to-eye, but it has the occasion when it is necessary to be able to do so.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, I want to be clear about that.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I presume that is the Member's main point.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: SPH, its current chairman is Dr Lee Boon Yang and he is a former Cabinet Minister.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In SPH's history, they have had other Chairpersons who have either been ex-senior civil servants or ex-Cabinet Ministers.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mediacorp's Chairman today is an ex-senior civil servant.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think, in that regard, Mr Khaw Boon Wan is held in high standing in Singapore and also by many beyond Singapore.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: He has a proven track record of taking on difficult issues and working on them.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: What you need is someone at the leadership level who has the gravitas, has the strategic vision and the experience in undertaking these sort of major tasks.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: As I said, it was a discussion that we had.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This is not the kind of position for which we have a very long shortlist or that we would do a global search.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In the end, you have to decide on the basis of what is needed, what are the attributes we seek and how do we go forward.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think what would be a missed opportunity is, if we allow political considerations to prevent us from making the right decision, in terms of the right person for the job, to get it done.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think that is what we have sought to do.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: But, as said by the Minister, it is no panacea.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: I have two clarifications to ask of the Minister, building on some of the questions earlier raised by the Member Jessica Tan.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: First, how will SPH maximise this opportunity for a fresh start?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: This will likely have to be consumer paid because advertising is not going to cut it.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: The fundamental source of competitive advantage here has become distribution and it has moved to the digital giants.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: And with what technology to support all this?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: How can you operate at a drastically lower level of cost in order to make money, including, for example, by moving to much more green-field tech platforms?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: I recognise these are questions for the CLG, but I think what I would like to know is: is there an ambition within the CLG to think of SPH now more as a start-up to benefit from this fresh start, rather than incremental thinking?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: How will the new entity be able to attract a visionary CEO in addition to talented journalists and editors but also tech people who see the noble mission of providing quality, independent journalism?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: In particular, can a bigger voice or a greater role be accorded to the internal staff, some of whom I know, have been pushing for change for a long time and love their jobs as SPH journalists in spite of the business uncertainty and in spite of all the accusations that they have partisan motives?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: They could have really good ideas under bold and inspiring leadership.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Because as Joseph Pulitzer once said, "Our republic and its press will rise or fall together." So, we do need solutions that enable high quality, independent journalism, not least local news and vernacular news, informing the communities about the events and people affecting their lives.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Minister, would you like to reply to those clarifications?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Because in discussing this – the merits, the challenges, the concerns and so on – I think we must not lose sight of the fact that this is an opportunity for the organisation and the people within to embark on the journey that they have travelled on up to now, but with a new beginning.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In considering that, I do want to make the point because the Member said, "Will this CLG behave like a start-up or will there be just incremental change?" I think the best way I would put it is this.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: You want the zest, the energy, the drive, the invention of a start-up, but you do not want to lose the credibility, the trust, the quality, the people that we have nurtured all through these years.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, we want to have our cake and eat it.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We want to be able to do both.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And I think it is very important that we recognise that because it is not about jettisoning everything and starting from scratch.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But neither is it about being so hidebound that we are not prepared to discard some of the older or long-held propositions from a business point of view in order to pursue new ideas.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, I think we need a bit of both, or rather we need a lot of both.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This is where I think, as the Member has mentioned, the staff, the people who are within, are just as important as the people who are without to be brought in, in due course, to complement the capability of the organisation.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The people who have been with the organisation – the journalists, the editors, the other staff – they bring a very valuable perspective.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think that has to be a part of the equation going forward, just as we need to bring in, whether it is technology-oriented people but also others who will be able to contribute and complement.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Therefore, I think the most important thing here is having a team; a team that brings together the best capabilities in order to maximise the chance of success for this new CLG venture.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think this is something Mr Khaw Boon Wan and I am sure the team, would be very seized with, including the process of finding not just an appropriate CEO but filling other talent requirements within the organisation.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The Member raised another very important point which pertains to the vernacular media.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This is an important part of what my colleague Mr Edwin Tong has called the tapestry of Singapore society.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We have to make sure that we pull that and ensure that that remains an important part of the overall entity that is the CLG and all its news media operations.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, we would want to be very clear about this aspect.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But how they achieve it is a different matter.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: If I can put it another way, the Member's questions revolved around: what are they going to do?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Whom are they going to do it for?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: What price are they going to impose and the financial model?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: All of these are very important questions but they are not questions that the Government should be answering.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Because ultimately, we have to put it to the Board and management, and for them to come back and tell us exactly what they have in mind, what are the pivots and changes, maybe even the reinvention they envisage.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And, in that context, what we need to do or what we can do – from the Government – to support.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: It looks like many Members want to be part of this narrative, this important narrative.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: I ask for the Members to keep their clarifications short so that I can call on both sides of the House and give each Member who wants to speak a chance to speak.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: So, very briefly, as we have been enjoined to do, I think with this latest move, the Government seems to acknowledge that commercially, it is very challenging to run a media operation, hence, the transition to the CLG structure.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Given this context and given the NPPA regime where broadsheet newspapers need to obtain NPPA licences, going forward, will the Government consider practising a light touch in awarding licences to Singaporean-owned companies who feel that they might want to enter this space and give it a go?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Because, they feel that they can innovate and somehow overcome these commercial hurdles as some media organisations in other parts of the world, like The Guardian in the UK, for example, have done.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: And lastly, I would just like to ask a question about how senior editorial appointments in the new CLG will be made.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: In his memoirs, the former chief of SPH, Mr Cheong Yip Seng wrote on page 432, and I quote, "the Newspaper and Printing Presses Act gives the Government veto powers over who gets to edit newspapers".

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: He is referring to his experience some time ago.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I asked a Parliamentary Question more recently about whether the Government plays a role in newspaper editorial —

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Perera, could you just ask your clarification?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: So, it appears that the Government does not.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: My question would be: would the Minister consider creating a structure within the CLG to ensure that senior editorial appointments are seen to be independent and safeguarded from any kind of influence whatsoever, and that is seen to be the case?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The first is NPPA and whether we would have a light touch and allow more entries into the market.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: First of all, I think when we are addressing this, let us diagnose the situation correctly.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: As I said, the issue is not around NPPA or no NPPA restrictions.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It is not around Government funding or not Government funding.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It is actually a circumstance that is the result of technological trends which have now made the financial model of this business of the news media a much more challenging one.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, we need to address that squarely, first.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But can we allow more entries into the market?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think we have a fairly vibrant news media.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I am not sure that they are all going to be in the traditional mode.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Members would know, for example, that we have some newer players, like Mothership, Rice Media and so on.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And I think what we are essentially saying is that, you have to look at it as an overall eco-system and it is an eco-system where we will have new entrants coming in.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: You will also have some of our traditional mainstream media – in this case, Mediacorp as well as SPH Media.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And we also have the international media who have a very strong presence here in Singapore.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, we have to look at it from an eco-system perspective.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It is not about singularly pursuing one aspect, but it is trying to ensure the overall local media grows and is able to hold its own vis-a-vis some of the broader competition it faces and the challenges we have talked about.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, that is the context in which I think we will look at it.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: If I could refer the Member back to what I have said in my earlier comments not just in my Ministerial Statement but subsequently.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In fact, that has been one of the key things we look at.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, as I have said, it is not just what Singaporeans say – which is important – in surveys and so on.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It is also what they do in terms of which sites do they go to, how many page views are they getting, what is the dwell time and so on?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: These are all metrics and I think the Member would be very aware that there are various metrics that can be used in order to measure this, the engagement of the audience.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And this is certainly something that we would want to ensure is achieved.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And if people do not trust our local media as a credible source of information, then I think these metrics will suffer.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I wanted to just make one clarification on senior editorial appointments.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: First, we know that journalists play a critical role in society and nation-building.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My second clarification in Malay, please, Sir, adding on to my hon colleague Ms Mariam Jaafar's question earlier.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In Malay):   Local papers like Berita Harian play an important role as a source of news and information for our community, especially for our senior citizens and they highlight stories of pride, interest and concern to the community.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I share – and I think we all do – the desire to ensure that our journalists continue to be able to pursue rewarding, fulfilling careers in this very important profession.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Indeed, we want to ensure that that continues to be the case even after this restructuring.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I also believe that the desire is more to build on the capabilities that we have and to see how we can attract new talent to augment what is already in there.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, I think the first order of business for the Chairman and the CLG Board and management would really be, amongst other things, as I have said in response earlier to Ms Jessica Tan, that it is not just about the business aspects and the financial aspects, but it is also about the people aspects and this must be given importance.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And this is something that, from the Government's perspective, we think is critical because, to reiterate a point I made earlier, it does not make sense to talk about quality journalism if you do not have the quality journalists and editors in the newsrooms.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: On the vernacular media – and I think the Member's point was specifically about the Malay media – I, again, want to reiterate the response that I gave earlier to Ms Mariam Jaafar.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Essentially, the vernacular media are a key part of our news media in Singapore because of the voice it gives to the different communities, no matter their size, and, through that, giving them a say and a visible participation in the common space.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Now, how the vernacular media evolves, what path they take, that, I think, is something we should have a more open mind about because, in the end, they have to adapt to the needs of the community, the needs of their readers, and work out a model that sustains the interest and earns the trust of the communities they serve.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: I will allow two more clarifications: Mr Pritam Singh and then closing with Ms Tin Pei Ling.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Just following up from my first list of clarifications.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I asked about the time when the Government first informed SPH that it was prepared to extend grants to support its media business and I also asked about the size of that grant.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The Minister made a point about the standards of journalism.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: It is not a simple issue to address in the course of a Ministerial Statement.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: But my generation, at least, remember this headline, this cover page in the New Paper, which was in 1997, at a very sensitive time just during the elections.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: It contained a checklist to help you decide how to vote.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The Minister spoke earlier about objectivity and balance.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The only thing objective about this cover page is the EPL scores – no-win for Liverpool and also for Manchester United.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The checklist, essentially, told the voters what you are voting for.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: If you vote for the PAP, you are voting for upgrading, Edusave and Members of Parliament of acceptable character.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Pritam Singh, if I could ask you to ask your clarification rather than expound in a speech.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: But I would agree with the Minister to the extent that one has to be fair to the journalists because there are good journalists.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And a good example can be found in a piece published on 1 May this year.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The Chinese Media Group head of Zaobao, Lee Huay Leng asked some very serious questions about the leadership transition to the 4G leadership and, she said, "internal competition is intense; there is no consensus to pick any one".

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I note the comment the Minister made about the surveys.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: But I think this is an opportunity to hear from the public and I hope the Government can consider this favourably.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Even in the examples that he cites, in a way, he has already illustrated the point that I am making.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: He went back to 1997 to bring out an example and then he says, just this year, the Chinese media put one point of view and the English media put another point of view.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Is this not the diversity that we want?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Is it not the diversity that the Leader of the Opposition has been talking about?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, I am not very clear why he thinks the current model is not succeeding.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I would challenge him to show me a model that works and that is perfect.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But is it one that works in our context?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And even in the examples that the Leader of the Opposition cites, I think it is quite clear.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And I would add that what we want at the end of the day is not posturing, but substance.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, if we can achieve that, not just in the news media, but also in this Chamber, I think we would have gone a long way to building a stronger country and nation.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: As for the funding, the Leader of the Opposition asked for ballpark numbers.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But that is precisely the problem, is it not?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think we should be talking about these sorts of matters when we have greater clarity because, to throw a ballpark number, and if I give Members a range, then the question would be, "Oh, it is a very big range.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Can you narrow it down?" And if I say, "No, I cannot", then we go back to square one.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, the point is we are doing the responsible thing here, from the Government's point of view.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But let us not miss the wood for the trees.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It is not about the details right now.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It is about the overall thrust of what we are trying to do.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Is our news media an important public good that we should be supporting?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And, if so, has it done a good job up to now in the models that we have used?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And, if yes, then let us work with that and build on it rather than talk about a complete wholesale overhaul.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Two clarifications, the first one in Mandarin, please.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: (In Mandarin):   Bilingualism is an important characteristic of our education system.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Being bilingual helps us to stay connected with our mother tongue cultures and it strengthens Singapore's global role as a cultural and economic bridge.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Hence, it is crucial to ensure that the high standards of our vernacular newspapers are maintained.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Lianhe Zaobao has won a hard-earned international award, let us continue to support them.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: I hope that the Minister can give us more information on this.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: (In English): The second point is about establishing Singapore's thought leadership and mindshare internationally.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Helping our papers to be able to be circulated internationally is a very critical part, in addition to the national cohesion, national public good in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: So, again, I would like to ask Minister, whether this is something that is on the agenda or one of the parameters that we may require the new CLG to look into in the move ahead.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: And whether there will be resources or funding set aside to build such capabilities?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Establishing Singapore's thought leadership and mindshare internationally is important.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: They are important pillars in our multi-ethnic fabric.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think I have made the point about the important role that they play, and in particular, by giving voice to the particular community.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: For that reason alone, we should be focused on how we can give them not just resources, but really the motivation and ambition to be more.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think that is the other point that the Member has raised, which is from an international point of view.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: For example, and I think specifically in the context of say, the Chinese media, I am sure it will not be lost on many within the SPH organisation but also those who are going to be involved later, that our Chinese media has significant potential to not just cater to the needs of Singaporeans, but also to be able to present a perspective on international affairs.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think it will be a very valued one because it will represent the Singapore point of view, which would be seen as being objective.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And it will also be one that would be valuable to Singaporeans because there will be a chance to understand some of these international developments through the lens of Singaporeans and how they assess this in terms of its impact on us and our long-term interests.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, for all those reasons, I think we will want to make sure that the vernacular media do not just pivot to digital, but actually develop additional important capabilities to meet this broader need that we have.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think this is something that I would have to defer to the CLG Chairman and the members of the Board and the management, who will then have to take this forward.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But I think from a Government point of view, certainly there should be no doubt as to where we stand on the issue.
